title: Accumulative selection is the predominant cause of change in domestic races

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Accumulative selection is the predominant cause of change in domestic races

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Among the causes of change in domestic races, including conditions of life, use and disuse, correlation and crossing, the accumulative action of selection, whether methodical or unconscious, is by far the predominant power.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Over all these causes of Change I am convinced that the accumulative action of Selection, whether applied methodically and more quickly, or unconsciously and more slowly, but more efficiently, is by far the predominant Power.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter I, “Variation under Domestication”; section “Summary”. Scope: domesticated animals and cultivated plants

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch01-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.53

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Selection signatures are widespread, but a common causal accounting across all domestic plants and animals is not available. Existing data can evaluate predominance in individual lineages only.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across domestic lineages, partition phenotypic change among selection, drift, environment, use, correlation and crossing using genomic time series and pedigrees. Selection explaining a clearly larger share than each rival supports predominance.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Representative historical time series are scarce.

Causal components overlap and are not additive.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.44
analysis feasibility: 0.48
data existence: 0.7
data adequacy: 0.4

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Genomic differentiation and crop evaluation data can show that selection has left a large mark on major domestic races, which addresses only part of a ranking among causes. The other causes are poorly collocated in the same records, so the predominance claim stays under-identified. Several decompositions are possible, and any one of them would take substantial harmonization for a handful of species.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Decompose among-breed phenotypic and genomic differences into components attributable to selection response, direct environmental effects, correlated response, and hybrid ancestry. Selection would be the predominant power if its component exceeded the sum of the others across a representative set of races; a larger share for conditions, use, correlation, or crossing would count against that ranking.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Selection scans detect some selected loci and miss polygenic and environmental change.

There is no agreed scale on which to add 'power' across selection, climate, use, correlation, and crossing.

Plastic responses to rearing conditions are rarely measured in the same animals as breed genomics.

data adequacy: 0.36
data existence: 0.52
